correctness.rationale: For any invertible structure matrix, independent squares force monomial automorphisms. Exact coefficient comparison gives t_i a_ij=t_j² a_{σ(i)σ(j)}. A nonidentity diagonal candidate forces a zero in every column; a permutation of support k moves k(2n-k) entry coordinates and permits at most half that many free orbit variables. Count fixed matrices, divide by |GL_n(F_q)|≥γ_q q^{n²}, sum nonidentity candidates, then apply Markov/union bound and Burnside, including uniform-orbit weighting. Split k≤n/2 and k>n/2 to obtain O_q((1-1/q)^n+n²q^{-n/2}). Proof includes every q>=3 and n>=2; exact finite checks q,n=(2,2),(2,3),(3,2),(3,3),(5,2),(2,4) passed and verify fixed-point equations, rank, class counts, rational bounds. These are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural exact isomorphism-class invariant previously given by an unwieldy orbit sum is resolved asymptotically for every fixed q>=3, with an explicit quantified error. Proves two genuinely distinct probabilistic statements—uniform labeled matrices and uniform isomorphism classes—and resolves a motivated perfect-stratum special case of surveyed asymptotic enumeration and typical-symmetry directions. Not an arbitrary finite slice or normalization exercise.
